text:
Marathon Petroleum fell 1.23% today, extending a two-week decline, as traders grappled with conflicting signals about U.S. refinery margins. The key headwind is news that the Trump administration is "very seriously" considering a diesel export ban to address global supply shortages—a move analysts warn could backfire by raising global diesel prices and forcing U.S. refiners to adjust production, potentially squeezing their profit margins on fuel sales. Meanwhile, refineries are already running at 94% capacity with substantial diesel and gasoline inventories on hand, leaving little room for output swings.

The geopolitical backdrop adds uncertainty: escalating U.S.-Iran tensions could disrupt Middle Eastern crude supplies, which would normally support refiner margins by widening the gap between crude cost and fuel prices. But if an export ban actually passes, it would flip that dynamic by capping what refiners can sell abroad at premium prices, offsetting any benefit from tighter global markets.
